## LU decomposition, back substitution and inverse (`ludcmp`, `lubksb`, `luminv`) {#sec-ch10-lu}

### Summary

The least-squares solvers factor their systems once and then solve. kintera keeps a Crout LU decomposition with
implicit (row-scaled) partial pivoting for this, adapted from the Numerical Recipes routines. The kernel accepts a
mask of rows to skip and a pivot tolerance, and it allocates its scratch space from a caller-supplied memory pool.
Back substitution and a column-by-column inverse use the factored matrix.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $\mathsf P \mathsf A = \mathsf L \mathsf U$ and solves with it, @eq-ch10-lu-crout.

**Data.** Row-major $n \times n$ array, overwritten by $\mathsf L$ and $\mathsf U$; permutation `indx`.

**Placement.** Inside `leastsq_kkt` (@sec-ch10-kkt) and `leastsq`.

**Activation.** Always; `pivot_tolerance` defaults to 0, `skip_row` to none.

**Guarantee / limits.** Returns 0 for a singular matrix; no condition estimate.

**Evidence.** Through the `leastsq_kkt` tests; see the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathsf A$, an $n \times n$ matrix with entries $a_{ij}$; $\mathsf L$, unit lower triangular;
$\mathsf U$, upper triangular; $\mathsf P$, the row permutation; $s_i$, the inverse of the largest $|a_{ij}|$ in row
$i$; $\tau$, the pivot tolerance.

### Derivation

Crout's method computes, column by column, the entries $u_{ij}$ of $\mathsf U$ on and above the diagonal
($i \le j$) and the entries $\ell_{ij}$ of $\mathsf L$ below it ($i > j$):

$$
\begin{aligned}
u_{ij} &= a_{ij} - \sum_{k < i} \ell_{ik}\, u_{kj} \\
\ell_{ij} &= \frac{1}{u_{jj}} \Big( a_{ij} - \sum_{k < j} \ell_{ik}\, u_{kj} \Big)
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch10-lu-crout}

Before the division, the row with the largest scaled candidate $s_i \big| a_{ij} - \sum_{k<j} \ell_{ik} u_{kj} \big|$
is swapped into the pivot position. The factorization is refused when that largest scaled value is not above
$\tau$. @eq-ch10-lu-crout is computed in `ludcmp` ({{< code src/math/ludcmp.h ludcmp >}}). A solve then runs forward
substitution with $\mathsf L$ and back substitution with $\mathsf U$ in `lubksb`
({{< code src/math/lubksb.h lubksb >}}). Exact in exact arithmetic.

### Numerical method

1. `ludcmp` records $s_i$ for every row; a row of zeros ends it with return value 0.
2. Columns are processed left to right. The pivot test is relative: `vv[i] * fabs(sum)` must exceed
   `pivot_tolerance`, so with the default 0 only an exactly zero pivot fails.
3. The return value is the permutation sign, $\pm 1$, or 0 for a singular matrix. `indx[j]` holds the row swapped
   into position $j$.
4. Rows and columns flagged in `skip_row` are left out of the factorization and of the solve; `leastsq_kkt` uses this
   for all-zero rows of its KKT[^rg-8c02b98e6297] block.
5. `lubksb` skips the leading zeros of the right-hand side: it starts the forward sum at the first nonzero entry.
6. `luminv` solves for the unit vectors one column at a time.

Scratch space comes from `pmalloc` and `pool_rewind` on the `work` pool; its size is `ludcmp_space`
({{< code src/utils/alloc.h ludcmp_space >}}). The figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| factorization | {{< code src/math/ludcmp.h ludcmp >}} | `ludcmp` | `pivot_tolerance`, `skip_row` |
| substitution | {{< code src/math/lubksb.h lubksb >}} | `lubksb` | `skip_row` |
| inverse | {{< code src/math/luminv.h luminv >}} | `luminv` | always |
| unconstrained least squares | {{< code src/math/leastsq.h leastsq >}} | `leastsq` | always |

: Code map of the LU kernels. {#tbl-ch10-lu-code}

`leastsq` ({{< code src/math/leastsq.h leastsq >}}) solves $\min \lVert \mathsf A x - b \rVert$ through the normal
equations $\mathsf A^{\mathrm T} \mathsf A\, x = \mathsf A^{\mathrm T} b$ with `ludcmp` and `lubksb`.

{{< code tests/test_thermo.cpp >}} also holds `test_ludcmp_skip`, a function that prints a result for a skipped
row; it is not a gtest case, and its call in `main` is commented out. No run record is attached in this draft
(missing evidence).

### Limits

- The doc comment of `ludcmp` says `indx` "outputs as +/- 1"; in the code the sign is the return value and `indx`
  holds row indices ({{< code src/math/ludcmp.h ludcmp >}}).
- `leastsq` ignores the return value of `ludcmp`, so a singular $\mathsf A^{\mathrm T} \mathsf A$ is solved with an
  incomplete factorization (read from the code; not tested). `leastsq` and `luminv` have no caller outside `src/math`
  at the pin.
- The normal equations square the condition number of $\mathsf A$.
